The gist of it is that monounsaturated fats are more stable, polyunsaturated fats are not stable. Most processed oils are polyunsaturated, and while yes they can be healthy, they are not as sold. These oils have deodorizers so you never know if they're rancid or not, and light destabilizes them further.

This is why expensive oils come in dark bottles, or completely metal containers, to prevent light from damaging the polyunsaturated fats and making the oil rancid.

When reading labels ideally you want poly and mono unsaturated fats to have a 1:1 ratio, however most Americans have these ratios all wrong and heavily biased towards the polyunsaturated side. These unstable oils are more likely to release free radicals.

Foods like hemp seed, and sesame seed have the perfect balance between poly and mono unsaturated fats, and are incredibly healthy for you. If you want to maintain a good balance naturally you need to eat fish like sardines, or other fatty fish with omega 3, which is a mono unsaturated fat, and combine it with walnuts which are rich in omega 6 or poly unsaturated fats.

I hope that sheds some light.
